questions.q: What is the one required setting on a Loop element?
options: A Decision outcome
A Collection Variable — what the loop iterates over
An API endpoint
A Default Outcome
questions.explain: The Loop element has exactly one required setting: the Collection Variable it runs each value from.

questions.q: What does 'Current Item from Loop' hold?
options: The total count of items in the collection
The very first item in the collection, for the entire loop
Whichever record or value the loop is currently processing, on that iteration
A static copy of the collection made before the loop started
questions.explain: Current Item from Loop is reset each iteration to hold the record currently being processed.

questions.q: Why is it bad practice to put an Update Records element inside a loop over a large collection?
options: Update Records elements can't be used in loops at all
It doesn't run in the correct order
Each Update Records run counts as a DML operation, and a flow is limited to 150 of them — looping multiplies that count
It makes the canvas too visually cluttered
questions.explain: Flows are limited to 150 DML operations; an Update Records element inside a loop can multiply that count past the limit.

questions.q: In the corrected pattern from this lesson (Get Active Users, UserLoop, Decision, Assignment, Update Records), what does the Assignment element inside the loop actually do?
options: It saves the changed value directly to the database
It only changes the current item's value in memory — nothing is saved until Update Records runs
It deletes the current user record
It triggers a second, nested loop
questions.explain: Assignment elements change values in memory only; the Update Records element after the loop is what commits the changes.

questions.q: Where should a Get Records element sit, relative to a loop that processes its results?
options: Inside the For Each path
Inside the After Last path
Before the loop, so it runs once instead of once per item
It can be placed anywhere; position has no effect on limits
questions.explain: Get Records should run once, before the loop starts, rather than being placed inside the loop where it would run per item.
